questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Stop completely at dangerous intersections.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
Some turning movements are allowed from certain lanes.
Both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisles next to handicapped parking spaces?
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicapped access aisles. These spaces are for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Can only vehicles with disability plates or placards park in reserved disability spaces?
questions.explanation: Only vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards can use spaces marked for persons with disabilities.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams so other drivers can see your vehicle clearly at night.

questions.question: Stopping completely, letting cross traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceeding when safe matches which light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to others, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: Sit at least 10 inches away from the steering wheel.
Tilt the steering wheel down so the airbag points at your chest, not your head or neck.

questions.explanation: Wear your seatbelt, sit at least 10 inches from the steering wheel, and tilt the wheel down if possible. These steps keep you safe with airbags.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive poorly, similar to drunk drivers. Coffee, windows, and loud radio do not fix drowsiness. Anyone can get drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop and wait for cars and pedestrians to clear before going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Stay on the right and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens, move as far to the right as you can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: Virginia's curfew laws prohibit drivers under 18 from driving from:
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot drive between midnight and 4 a.m., with some exceptions.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: If someone has consumed alcohol, what will help them overcome its effects?
questions.explanation: Only time allows a person to recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Using a radar detector is illegal in Virginia.
questions.explanation: Virginia law prohibits the use of radar detectors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells drivers to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop. Yield to other drivers and pedestrians. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead is now a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake hard to force them to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors constantly for tailgaters or fast-approaching vehicles. If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, a right turn is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a greater crash risk when using which of these?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player takes your attention off the road. All of these can distract you and increase your crash risk.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another car?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You cannot cross these lines to pass. The only exception is when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes your car harder to control.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.
